subject.title: [Feature] Pre-response enforcement hooks (hard gates) for mandatory tool-call / policy rules

question: Should OpenClaw add a versioned fail-closed final-response gate, and what core/plugin API should own mandatory tool accounting, validator execution, retry/fallback, audit, and plugin trust semantics?
rationale: The source-proven gap is real, but the solution defines a security boundary and compatibility-sensitive plugin/runtime contract that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Design a versioned response-gate API
options.body: Keep the issue open and require maintainer design review before implementing a core/plugin seam with contract tests and upgrade-safe defaults.

options.title: Scope to existing hooks only
options.body: Document current before_tool_call, before_agent_finalize, message_sending, and reply_dispatch capabilities as adjacent controls and close the broader two-phase gate as not planned.

options.title: Split into narrower issues
options.body: Track mandatory-tool ledger, final-response validators, audit, and public-action approval as separate canonical work items before any implementation PR.

recommendation.title: Design a versioned response-gate API
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and require maintainer design review before implementing a core/plugin seam with contract tests and upgrade-safe defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a security/product boundary decision and recent adjacent audit-policy work makes this the best available owner signal.
